roleInterpretation: Own Veilwild runtime telemetry/evidence instrumentation and the claim-specific Player Evidence/Human Playtest process, including evidence transport and condition binding. Do not own producer semantics, product authority, Red-Team judgment, accessibility authority, or Human participant truth.
standingRationale: The exact baseline contains a current Player Evidence Programme, generic replay/evidence infrastructure, and passing evidence-boundary tests, but no Veilwild-specific telemetry contract, runtime event emission, durable condition-bound evidence artifact, frozen Player Evidence Contract, or real participant evidence.
topFalsifiers: Veilwild runtime cannot emit or durably retain the minimum player-facing event set needed to attribute cue/state/detection/escape/observation outcomes.
Producer semantic drift causes telemetry names or payloads to stop matching A02 cue semantics, A13 creature-state semantics, A25 observe-action semantics, or A17 runtime/build identity.
Evidence records omit exact source/build/condition identity, making later Human or QA evidence stale, ambiguous, or non-transportable.
Instrumentation changes timing, input behavior, cue visibility, or other player-facing consequences enough to contaminate the condition being measured.
The Human protocol fails to bind a concrete decision/claim/population/context/method/measure/decision rule before exposure, allowing post-hoc metric storytelling.
Synthetic, expert, mechanical, or Agent-generated observations are represented as Human outcome evidence.
Unnecessary participant-identifying data is collected or retained despite a local/minimal evidence path being sufficient.
expectedInputs: A01/F01: exact decision/product-loop claims that Human evidence may later inform, without delegating product authority.
A02/F02: cue vocabulary, intended cue meanings, onboarding/session milestones, and player-facing claim statements.
A13/F13: creature-state transition vocabulary and runtime state identifiers.
A16/F16: interactive/spatial audio cue event semantics where they are part of the declared information budget.
A17/F17: runtime integration hook, scene/run identity, monotonic clock/tick source, source revision and frozen candidate/build identity.
A19/F20: reproducible build/artifact identity and exact run condition metadata.
A22/F23: accessibility conditions/settings that materially qualify participant condition and telemetry interpretation.
A25/F18: player input/observe-action, detection/false-detection, feedback and success/failure event semantics.
A23/F25: frozen-candidate admission/QA receipts needed before any Human-ready standing is asserted.
expectedOutputs: Veilwild telemetry/evidence event contract with stable event names, required fields, units, condition identity, failure modes and validation oracle.
Runtime-consumable durable telemetry/evidence sink or adapter that preserves ordered events and exact build/run identity without claiming Human truth.
Claim-specific Veilwild Player Evidence Contract and Human playtest protocol with explicit Human-UNKNOWN guards.
Evidence transport/replay validation that proves raw event records can be traced to exact runtime/build condition.
A21 handoff interfaces for A02/A17/A19/A22/A23/A25 and any producer whose state/cue identifiers enter evidence records.
highestRiskBoundaryAssumption: A21 can instrument the real Godot candidate through stable producer-owned state/action interfaces while preserving exact build/condition identity, without inventing upstream semantics or converting instrumentation completeness into Human standing; the actual Human participant remains an external evidence source.
scopeSplitAssessment: NO_SPLIT_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION. F22 and F24 share the same evidence identity/condition-binding boundary and can remain one A21 role. The real Human participant is external evidence, not an Agent/front to self-activate. Revisit only if a distinct repeated instrumentation-vs-research process bottleneck develops with separate stable inputs/outputs/oracles.
externalAuthorityNotes: ISO 9241-11:2018 remains current (confirmed 2023) and treats usability as an outcome for specified users/goals/context of use.
ISO 9241-210:2019 remains current (confirmed 2025) and supports human-centred design activities throughout the interactive-system lifecycle.
ICO UK GDPR guidance emphasizes purpose limitation and data minimisation; local R1 telemetry should avoid collecting participant-identifying data unless necessary for the declared evidence purpose.
